notes: The bēon forms (bēo, bīst, bīþ, bēoþ) express permanent or habitual truths and future certainty. The wesan forms (eom, eart, is, sind) express immediate or contingent states. The bēon form first appears in Ōsweald Bera Ch. 3.

Suppletive form of bēon. Wesan supplies the infinitive, present participle (wesende), and imperative (wes / wesaþ). The eom/eart/is forms in the present indicative and all wæs/wǣre past forms belong to this paradigm. See bēon.
